subject.title: [Feature]: Support arbitrary workspace files in bootstrap context injection

question: Should OpenClaw accept explicitly configured custom-basename workspace files as part of the core `bootstrap-extra-files` hook contract, or keep the hook limited to recognized workspace bootstrap filenames?
rationale: The code change is mechanically narrow, but it changes deterministic prompt context admission and the public hook contract, which is a maintainer product/security boundary decision.

options.title: Approve guarded custom basenames
options.body: Allow explicitly configured workspace-relative custom basenames through the existing hook path after preserving boundary checks, budgets, diagnostics, docs, and session filtering.

options.title: Keep recognized basenames only
options.body: Reject arbitrary configured bootstrap files and continue requiring users to map deterministic startup context into the current recognized workspace file model.

options.title: Defer to broader context API
options.body: Keep this issue open until a broader workspace context/discovery convention decides how custom context files should be surfaced.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded custom basenames
recommendation.body: Allow explicitly configured workspace-relative custom basenames through the existing hook path after preserving boundary checks, budgets, diagnostics, docs, and session filtering.

likelyOwner.reason: The boundary-safe bootstrap read and hook-security history make this the clearest product/security routing candidate among the code-history owners found.
